summary: Manchester City have reportedly offered £120m for Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson, who is preparing for the World Cup with England.
content_text: Elliot Anderson will not be distracted by the prospect of a huge transfer to Manchester City after emerging as a key player for England in their World Cup preparations. That is the view of Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel, though the German is aware critics will focus on Anderson's price tag if he completes his move to the Etihad Stadium. Following two hugely impressive seasons at Nottingham Forest, Anderson is one of the Premier League's most in-demand players this summer. City have reportedly had two bids for his services turned down already, with the second of those offers being worth £120m including add-ons. The record fee for a British player is the £105m Arsenal paid to acquire Declan Rice from West Ham in 2023, but Forest are seemingly hoping to extract a figure that eclipses Liverpool's Premier League-record signing of Alexander Isak last year, which was worth £125m. Anderson is expected to play a key role alongside Rice at the World Cup, as England build towards their opening fixture against Croatia next Wednesday. And when asked if Anderson would be distracted by the reports of City's interest, Tuchel said: "No comment! He seems not to be affected.
